mainTopic: יהושע's ten conditions for the land of ישראל: what each one allows, and why the count is exactly ten
overview: This amud continues the list of conditions that יהושע set when the tribes received ארץ ישראל. These conditions are public rights that limit what a private owner can do with his land. They include not taking cuttings from the sunny side of a tree, letting the town use a brand-new spring for free, and fishing in the Sea of Tiberias without blocking boats. Other conditions allow relieving oneself behind a fence, walking on field paths, stepping off a rough road, cutting a way out of a vineyard when lost, and burying a מת מצוה where it is found. Along the way the גמרא tells stories about שמואל, רבי and רבי יהודה בן נקוסא stepping off the road. It also explains how the Torah duty of השבת גופו differs from יהושע's added permission to cut through vines. Then the גמרא checks the count of ten. Walking on private paths turns out to be שלמה's teaching, based on a verse in משלי. The rules of רבי יהודה and רבי ישמעאל are not counted, because the list includes only conditions all the חכמים accept.

steps.title: Not from the sunny side of the tree
steps.stepSummary: The last limit on taking cuttings from another person's tree: you may not cut from the side that faces the sun, because that side gives the best fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: But not from a place that faces the sun, as it says: 'And for the precious things of the fruits of the sun.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the list of limits on cutting shoots from someone else's tree. You may not cut from the part of the tree that faces the sun.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The public may take cuttings, but only in a way that does not hurt the owner's crop. The פסוק shows that the sun brings the best fruit. So the sunny side is off-limits, because cutting there would cause the owner a real loss.

keyTerms.meaning: The crops that the sun brings

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא מִמְּקוֹם שֶׁהוּא רוֹאֶה אֶת הַחַמָּה;
phrases.english: but not from a place that faces the sun,
as it is stated: 'And for the precious things of the fruits of the sun.'
phrases.notes: דברים 33:14

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא מִמְּקוֹם שֶׁהוּא רוֹאֶה אֶת הַחַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the details of the cutting condition from the previous section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cuttings may not be taken from the side of the tree that faces the sun.

steps.title: The town may use a brand-new spring
steps.stepSummary: Another condition of יהושע: if a new spring comes up on private land, the people of the town may draw water from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a spring that comes out for the first time: the people of the town may take water from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא lists the next condition. Even a spring that has just appeared on someone's land is open to the townspeople.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think a new spring belongs only to the owner of the land, since nobody has ever used it before. The condition says no: the town still has a right to it.

keyTerms.meaning: For the first time, brand new

phrases.english: And a spring that emerges for the first time:
the people of the city take supplies from it.
phrases.notes: Literally 'supply themselves': they may draw water from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next condition in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Townspeople may draw water from a new spring on private land.

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא: they must pay
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא adds that whoever draws from the new spring must pay the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא says: and he pays him money.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא adds a condition to the spring rule: the town may use the water, but it has to pay the owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his view the right of use is not free. The owner cannot stop the town, but he is paid for his water.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna says:
And he gives him money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a payment requirement to the spring rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Those who use the new spring must pay the owner.

steps.title: The halacha does not follow him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the הלכה is not like רבה בר רב הונא, so the water may be taken for free.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the halacha is not like him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides against רבה בר רב הונא. The town does not have to pay for the spring water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling turns the spring condition back into a free right. יהושע's condition gave the town full use of the water, not a right to buy it.

keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה is not like him

steps.whatToRemember: A new spring on private land is open to the town, and no payment is required.

phrases.english: But the halakha is not in accordance with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the payment requirement from step 3 for practical halacha.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The water may be drawn without paying.

steps.title: Fishing in the Sea of Tiberias
steps.stepSummary: Another condition of יהושע: anyone may fish in the Sea of Tiberias, but not with a blocking trap that stops boats. Nets and traps are fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And people may fish in the Sea of Tiberias, as long as one does not spread a fence-trap that stops the boats. But he may fish with nets and traps.
steps.whatsHappening: The next condition opens the Sea of Tiberias to everyone for fishing. It then limits how they may fish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fishing is allowed, but not in a way that harms other people. A large fence-like trap blocks boats, so it is forbidden. Regular nets and traps do not block traffic, so they are allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A fence-like barrier trap set in the water

phrases.english: And they may fish in the Sea of Tiberias,
provided that he does not spread a fence-trap
phrases.notes: A barrier stretched through the water to catch fish.

phrases.english: and so stop the boat.
But he may catch fish with nets and with traps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next condition in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anyone may fish in the Sea of Tiberias, but not with a barrier that blocks boats.

steps.title: The tribes themselves agreed to this
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that at the start the tribes made this same agreement with each other: no blocking traps, but nets and traps are allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: At first the tribes agreed with each other that no one may spread a fence-trap and stop the boats, but one may fish with nets and traps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up the fishing rule. It shows the rule was an agreement made among the tribes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording matches the fishing condition almost exactly. It adds the source: this was a deal the tribes made with each other at the beginning, so the rule rests on their shared agreement.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הִתְנוּ שְׁבָטִים זֶה עִם זֶה
phrases.english: Initially, the tribes stipulated with each other
that one may not spread a fence-trap
and so stop the boat,
but one may fish with nets and with traps.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הִתְנוּ שְׁבָטִים זֶה עִם זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the fishing condition with a ברייתא about an agreement among the tribes.
steps.raayaObject: The fishing rule in the Sea of Tiberias
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the original agreement among the tribes

steps.title: The sea belonged to נפתלי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the Sea of Tiberias was in the portion of נפתלי, and that נפתלי also got a strip of shore to its south, fulfilling the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: The Sea of Tiberias was in נפתלי's portion. And more than that, נפתלי took a strip the full length of a fishing-net rope on its south side, to fulfill the verse 'possess the sea and the south.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about who owned the sea. It belonged to the tribe of נפתלי, along with a strip of land on its southern shore.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains the background of the fishing condition. The sea really belonged to one tribe, and the condition gave everyone else the right to fish there. The extra southern strip matches the פסוק's blessing to נפתלי of 'sea and south.'

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but also
The rope of a fishing net
To fulfill what the פסוק says

steps.whatToRemember: The Sea of Tiberias belonged to נפתלי, yet יהושע's condition let everyone fish there, as long as they did not block the boats.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The Sea of Tiberias
was in the portion of Naphtali.
And not only that, but
he took the full length of a net's rope on its south side,
phrases.notes: 'He' means the tribe of נפתלי.

phrases.english: to fulfill that which is stated:
'Possess the sea and the south.'
phrases.notes: דברים 33:23

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יַמָּהּ שֶׁל טְבֶרְיָא בְּחֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל נַפְתָּלִי הָיְתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the background of the fishing condition: who actually owned the sea.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Sea of Tiberias and a strip of shore to its south belonged to נפתלי.

steps.title: Loose items belong to all tribes, attached items to the local tribe
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר teaches that loose items found in the mountains during the conquest belonged to all the שבטים, but attached things belonged to the tribe that received that land.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says that loose things in the mountains belong to all the tribes together, but things attached to the ground belong to that particular tribe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about who owned what in ארץ ישראל when the land was divided among the tribes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Loose items, like spoils left behind, were taken by the whole nation together, so they are shared. Attached items, like trees, are part of the land itself, so they go to whichever tribe received that land.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught in a ברייתא
Items attached to the ground, like trees

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
Detached things that are in the mountains
stand in the possession of all the tribes,
phrases.notes: He means items found loose when the land was conquered, so they count as shared spoils.

phrases.english: but attached things are in the possession of that tribe.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of how the land was divided among the tribes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Loose items in the mountains are shared by all tribes, and attached items belong to the tribe that owns the land.

steps.title: Every tribe received every type of terrain
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that every שבט got some mountain, lowland, south land, and valley, and proves it from a פסוק. The Canaanite nations before them also had the same mix.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no tribe in ישראל that did not get some land in the mountains, the lowland, the south, and the valley, as the פסוק says: 'Turn and journey, and go to the hill country of the Amorite and all its neighbors, in the plain, the mountain, the lowland, the south, and the seashore.' The same was true of the Canaanites, Perizzites, and Amorites before them, since it says 'and all its neighbors.' So all the neighbors had land like this.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and teaches that each tribe's portion included all kinds of land, then brings a פסוק as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why the earlier rule matters for every tribe: each one had mountains, so each one could have attached items in mountain areas. The words 'and all its neighbors' show that the nations living there before also each had all these types of land.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין לְךָ כׇּל שֵׁבֶט וְשֵׁבֶט מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: And you have no single tribe of Israel
that does not have land in the mountain and in the lowland
and in the south and in the valley,
as it is stated: 'Turn and journey,
phrases.notes: דברים 1:7

phrases.aramaic: וּבֹאוּ הַר הָאֱמוֹרִי וְאֶל כׇּל שְׁכֵנָיו;
phrases.english: and go to the hill country of the Amorite and to all its neighbors;
in the plain, in the mountain, in the lowland
and in the south and on the seashore, etc.'
And so you find with the Canaanites
and the Perizzites and the Amorites who were before them,
as it is stated: 'and to all its neighbors'
so we see that its neighbors were like this too.
phrases.notes: The neighbors are listed right next to all the land types, so each nation had every kind of land.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לְךָ כׇּל שֵׁבֶט וְשֵׁבֶט מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, adding that every tribe had mountain land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every tribe received mountain, lowland, south land, and valley, and this is learned from דברים 1:7.

steps.title: Relieving oneself behind a fence, even in a saffron field
steps.stepSummary: Another of יהושע's conditions: a person may relieve himself behind a fence, even in a field full of valuable saffron.
steps.simpleTranslation: And people may relieve themselves behind a fence, even in a field full of saffron.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the list of יהושע's conditions and quotes the next one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saffron is expensive, so you might think the owner could stop people from entering. יהושע's condition says the owner must allow it anyway.

phrases.english: And people may relieve themselves behind the fence,
even in a field that is full of saffron.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the tribal-ownership topic and returns to יהושע's list of conditions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anyone may relieve himself behind a fence in another person's field, even a saffron field.

steps.title: The real point: taking a stone from the fence
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב explains that the condition was only needed to allow taking a stone from the fence to clean oneself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: This was only needed to allow taking a stone from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב explains what new permission יהושע's condition really adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Relieving oneself when one must is obvious, so a special condition would not be needed for that. The new point is that you may even take a stone out of the owner's fence to clean yourself.

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לִיטּוֹל הֵימֶנּוּ צְרוֹר.
phrases.english: It was needed only to allow taking a stone from it.
phrases.notes: 'From it' means from the fence.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what new thing the condition in step 10 adds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The condition allows taking a stone from the owner's fence for cleaning oneself.

steps.title: Taking the stone is allowed even on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא adds that one may take such a stone even on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Even on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא adds that the permission to take a stone applies even on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally moving stones on שבת is a problem of מוקצה. Because of the importance of human dignity, רב חסדא allows taking the stone even on שבת.
steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא's reason, human dignity, does not appear in this line. It is the standard explanation for why moving the stone is allowed.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
And even on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רב אחא בר יעקב's permission to שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking a stone from the fence for this purpose is allowed even on שבת.

steps.title: מר זוטרא put the stone back and had it plastered
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא חסידא would take the stone and put it back, then tell his attendant to plaster it into place.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא the pious would take the stone and put it back, and he told his attendant (the next day): Go plaster it in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how a very pious רב acted when using this permission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר זוטרא used the permission, but went beyond the law. He returned the stone so the owner's fence would not be harmed, and had his attendant fix it firmly later.

keyTerms.meaning: The pious one, who goes beyond the letter of the law

phrases.english: Mar Zutra the Pious would take the stone and put it back,
and he would say to his attendant (the next day):
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. Either way, the plastering waited until after שבת.

phrases.english: Go plaster it in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a pious person's practice when using the permission from steps 11 and 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pious person returns the stone and later repairs the fence, beyond what the law requires.

steps.title: Walking on private field paths until the second rain
steps.stepSummary: Another of יהושע's conditions: people may walk on paths through private fields until the second rainfall of the season.
steps.simpleTranslation: And people may walk on private paths until the second rainfall comes down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next of יהושע's conditions, about walking through private fields.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shortcuts through a field cause no damage while the ground is dry. Once the second rain falls, crops start to grow and walking would harm them, so the right ends.

keyTerms.meaning: The second rainfall of the season

phrases.english: And people may walk on private paths,
until the second rainfall comes down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next condition of יהושע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anyone may walk on paths through private fields until the second rainfall.

steps.title: In Babylonia even dew makes walking harmful
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that for the fields in Babylonia, even dew makes walking on them damaging.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: And these fields of ours, even dew is bad for them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא limits the walking permission for the fields of his own land, Babylonia.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ארץ ישראל the cutoff is the second rain. Babylonian soil is different, so even night dew softens it enough that walking causes damage. When there is dew, the right to walk does not apply there.

keyTerms.meaning: Is bad for it, harms it

steps.whatToRemember: These conditions balance the owner's rights against public needs. You may relieve yourself and even take a stone from the fence, and you may walk on field paths, but only while no real damage is done. Step 33 will show that the walking rule actually comes from שלמה, not יהושע.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: וְהַאי דִּידַן – אֲפִילּוּ טַל קָשֵׁי לֵהּ.
phrases.english: And this land of ours, even dew is bad for it.
phrases.notes: 'Ours' means the fields in Babylonia, where רב פפא lived.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a local limit to the walking permission in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In Babylonia, after dew has fallen, walking on private field paths is harmful and not allowed.

steps.title: Stepping off a bad road onto the side fields
steps.stepSummary: Another condition of יהושע: travelers may walk on the private land at the sides of the road when the road itself has hard bumps.
steps.simpleTranslation: And people may step off to the sides of the roads because of the hard bumps in the roads.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next condition on יהושע's list. When a road is too rough to walk on, travelers may walk on the private fields along its edge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally walking on someone's field is not allowed. Here the land was given out from the start on condition that travelers may use its edges when the road is hard to walk on. So the owner never fully owned that right of way.

keyTerms.meaning: literally 'pegs'; hard bumps or rough spots in the road

phrases.english: And they may step off to the sides of the roads,
because of the hard bumps of the roads.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of יהושע's conditions after the רב פפא comment about fields in בבל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Travelers may walk on the private land along the road when the road has hard bumps.

steps.title: רב יהודה asks whether the conditions apply in Babylonia
steps.stepSummary: שמואל steps off the road in בבל, and רב יהודה asks whether יהושע's conditions apply there at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל and רב יהודה were walking on a road. שמואל stepped off to the side. רב יהודה asked him: do יהושע's conditions apply even in בבל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story in which שמואל uses the rule from the previous step while in בבל. רב יהודה asks whether that is allowed outside ארץ ישראל, which sets up שמואל's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהושע set these conditions when he divided ארץ ישראל among the tribes. So it seems they should only cover land in ארץ ישראל. רב יהודה wants to know why שמואל relied on them in בבל.

phrases.english: Shmuel and Rav Yehuda
were walking along the road,
and Shmuel stepped off to the sides of the road.
Rav Yehuda said to him:
The conditions that Yehoshua set,
do they apply even in Babylonia?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story showing the rule of step 16 in action, which raises a question about where the rule applies.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do יהושע's conditions apply to land outside ארץ ישראל?

steps.title: שמואל: the conditions apply even outside Israel
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that he holds יהושע's conditions apply even outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to him: I hold they apply even outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers רב יהודה's question. Yes, he holds the conditions apply even in חוץ לארץ, so he was allowed to step off the road.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל treats these conditions as basic rules for how land is held anywhere, not only for the land יהושע divided. That is why he could rely on them in בבל.

phrases.english: He said to him:
For I hold
that they apply even outside the Land of Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יהודה's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יהושע's conditions apply even outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.whyThisMatters: It widens the reach of יהושע's conditions beyond ארץ ישראל, at least according to שמואל.

steps.title: רבי notices a man striding on the road instead of stepping aside
steps.stepSummary: רבי and רבי חייא step off the road. רבי יהודה בן נקוסא keeps taking big steps on the road ahead of them, and רבי asks who is showing off in front of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי and רבי חייא were walking and stepped off to the sides of the road. רבי יהודה בן נקוסא was taking big steps along the road in front of them. רבי said to רבי חייא: Who is this who shows off his greatness in front of us?
steps.whatsHappening: A second story starts. Someone refuses to use the side fields and strides over the bumps instead, and רבי sees this as showing off. רבי's question sets up רבי חייא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stepping off the road is fully allowed. Avoiding it in front of greater rabbis can look as if one is acting holier than them. רבי reads the man's behavior as arrogance.

phrases.english: Rebbi and Rabbi Chiya
phrases.notes: Plain 'רבי' with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: were walking along the road,
and they stepped off to the sides of the road.
Taking big steps along the road
was Rabbi Yehuda ben Nekosa, in front of them.
phrases.notes: Some versions say קנוסא, in round brackets; the word in square brackets, נקוסא, is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: Rebbi said to Rabbi Chiya:
Who is this
who shows off his greatness in front of us?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי הוּא זֶה שֶׁמַּרְאֶה גְּדוּלָּה בְּפָנֵינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story about the same condition, this time about someone who does not use it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is this man acting more strictly than everyone else?

steps.title: רבי חייא defends his student
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא says it may be his student רבי יהודה בן נקוסא, whose actions are all לשם שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא said: Perhaps it is my student רבי יהודה בן נקוסא, and all his actions are for the sake of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא answers רבי's question. If this is his student, the man is not showing off but acting sincerely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same action can be arrogance or genuine piety, depending on who does it. רבי חייא vouches that this student's extra care is sincere.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya said to him:
Perhaps it is Rabbi Yehuda ben Nekosa,
my student,
and all his actions are for the sake of Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁמָּא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן נְקוֹסָא תַּלְמִידִי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי's question and defends the man's motives.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It may be רבי חייא's student, who acts sincerely and not out of pride.

steps.title: רבי accepts the student's sincerity, but warns him
steps.stepSummary: When רבי sees it really is רבי יהודה בן נקוסא, he says that anyone else would have been harshly punished.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they reached him, רבי saw him and said: If you were not יהודה בן נקוסא, I would have cut off your legs with iron shears.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. רבי lets this student off because he is known to be sincere, but makes clear that such behavior is normally out of place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's strong words show that being stricter than the הלכה in front of greater rabbis is usually seen as arrogance. Only this student's known sincerity protects him.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have cut them off

steps.whatToRemember: Stepping off a bad road is a right יהושע built into the land. Refusing to use it in front of greater people can look like showing off, unless you are known to be sincere.

phrases.english: When they reached him,
Rebbi saw him.
He said to him:
If you were not Yehuda ben Nekosa,
I would have cut off your legs
with iron shears.
phrases.notes: This is a picture, not a literal threat. He means he would have put him in נידוי for acting this way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָאו יְהוּדָה בֶּן נְקוֹסָא אַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story after רבי חייא's defense.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Acting more strictly than others in front of greater rabbis is normally improper; only a person known for sincerity is excused.

steps.title: A lost person may cut through vineyard branches
steps.stepSummary: Another condition of יהושע: someone lost among vineyards may cut through the branches to find his way out.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who gets lost among the vineyards may cut through branches going down and cut through branches going up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the list of יהושע's conditions. A person lost in vineyards may cut through the vines to reach the road again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting someone's vines is usually damage he would have to pay for. The land was given out on condition that a lost person may cut a path out, so this is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: cuts through branches to clear a way

phrases.english: One who gets lost among the vineyards
may cut through branches and go down,
cut through branches and go up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the stories, the גמרא returns to the list of יהושע's conditions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person lost in vineyards may cut through the vines to get out.

steps.title: A helper may also cut through to rescue someone lost
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds that someone who sees another person lost may also cut through the vines to bring him out, and so may the lost person himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One who sees his friend lost among the vineyards may cut through going up and going down until he brings him to the city or the road. And the same for the lost person himself: he may cut through until he reaches the city or the road.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא extends the condition from step 22. It covers a rescuer, not only the lost person, and says how far the permission goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new points are that a helper may also cut through, and that the permission lasts only until they reach the city or the road. After that, they may not cut any more vines.
steps.whatToRemember: Both the lost person and someone rescuing him may cut through vineyard branches, but only until they reach the city or the road.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who sees his friend lost among the vineyards
may cut through and go up, cut through and go down,
until he brings him up to the city or to the road.
And likewise, he himself who is lost among the vineyards
may cut through and go up, cut through and go down
until he comes up to the city or to the road.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָרוֹאֶה חֲבֵירוֹ תּוֹעֶה בֵּין הַכְּרָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the condition from step 22 to a rescuer and sets its limit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A rescuer or the lost person may cut through vines until reaching the city or the road.

steps.title: Why does the ברייתא need to say 'and similarly'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא added 'וכן' to include the lost person himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the point of saying 'and similarly'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא bothered to say that the lost person may also cut branches. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already allowed a rescuer to cut vines. Adding the lost person himself seems obvious, since he is the one in trouble. So why spell it out?

keyTerms.meaning: And similarly, the word that adds another case

phrases.english: What is the point of 'and similarly'?
phrases.notes: This points back to the last line of the ברייתא in step 23: 'and similarly, the lost person himself may cut through.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the extra clause in the ברייתא quoted in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the ברייתא needed to state that the lost person himself may cut branches.

steps.title: Even the lost person, who does not know the way, may cut through
steps.stepSummary: Without 'וכן' we might think only a rescuer, who knows where he is heading, may cut. The lost person would have to go back along the edges. The ברייתא teaches that he may cut too.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought that only the other person, who knows where he is going, may cut branches. But the lost person himself does not know where he is going, so he may not cut and must go back along the borders. The ברייתא teaches us that he may cut.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the הוה אמינא that 'וכן' is coming to reject.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rescuer sees the way out, so cutting through actually gets him somewhere. The lost person might just be cutting blindly and damaging vines for nothing. Even so, the ברייתא allows him to cut his way out.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
Along the boundaries or edges of the field
It teaches us (that the assumption is wrong)

phrases.english: You might have said:

phrases.aramaic: חֲבֵירוֹ הוּא דְּיָדַע לְהֵיכָא מְסַלֵּק – דְּנִיפְסוֹג;
phrases.english: it is the other person, who knows where he is going, who may cut branches;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הוּא, דְּלָא יֵדַע לְהֵיכָא קָא סָלֵיק –
phrases.english: but he himself, who does not know where he is going,
may not cut branches,
and he must go back around along the boundaries;
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean 'go around.'

phrases.english: so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'וכן' is needed to teach that the lost person, even though he does not know the way, may also cut through the vines.

steps.title: Returning a lost person is already a Torah law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: why did יהושע need to set up this condition, if the Torah already commands us to return a lost person?
steps.simpleTranslation: But this is a Torah law! As a ברייתא teaches: From where do we know that you must return a person's body (help a lost person)? The פסוק says 'and you shall return it to him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why יהושע needed to make a special rule for something the Torah already requires.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה of השבת אבידה includes helping a lost person find his way, based on the word 'והשבותו'. If the Torah already requires this, a condition from יהושע seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: From the Torah, a Torah law
Returning his body, meaning helping a lost person himself

phrases.english: But this is a Torah law!
As it is taught in a ברייתא: From where do we know the duty of returning his body?
phrases.notes: 'His body' means the lost person himself, not his belongings.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'And you shall return it'!
phrases.notes: דברים 22:2. The word can also be read as 'and you shall return him.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for יהושע's condition about lost people in vineyards.
steps.kashyaTarget: יהושע's condition allowing someone lost in vineyards to cut his way out.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rabbinic condition is unnecessary if the Torah already requires returning a lost person.

steps.title: The Torah allows only walking the edges; יהושע allowed cutting straight through
steps.stepSummary: The Torah only requires going around along the boundaries. יהושע added permission to cut branches and go straight up or down.
steps.simpleTranslation: By Torah law he must stay along the borders. יהושע came and enacted that he may cut branches going up and cut branches going down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that יהושע's condition adds something beyond the Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah obligation to help a lost person does not permit damaging someone else's vines. יהושע's condition allowed cutting through to take the most direct route out.
steps.whatToRemember: השבת גופו is a Torah law, but only by walking around the edges. Cutting through someone's vines to get out is allowed because of יהושע's condition.

phrases.english: By Torah law, he must stay along the boundaries;
he came and enacted
phrases.notes: 'He' is יהושע.

phrases.english: that one may cut branches and go up, cut branches and go down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the scope of the Torah law from the rabbinic addition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יהושע's condition repeats the Torah law of returning a lost person.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah law allows only walking the boundaries; יהושע added permission to cut through the vines.

steps.title: Next condition: a מת מצוה acquires its place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next condition of יהושע: a מת מצוה is buried where it is found.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a מת מצוה acquires its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next condition of יהושע. This sets up a contradiction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מת מצוה is a body with no one else to bury it. יהושע's condition says it may be buried right where it was found, even on someone else's land.

keyTerms.meaning: A dead body with no one to bury it
Acquires its place, meaning it is buried where it was found

phrases.english: And a מת מצוה acquires its place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the vineyard condition to the next condition of יהושע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מת מצוה is buried in the place where it is found.

steps.title: Contradiction: a body found on a road must be moved
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a body found on a main road should be moved to the side, and to a fallow field rather than a plowed one. That seems to contradict 'it acquires its place.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And they raised a contradiction: Someone who finds a dead body lying on a main road moves it to the right or left of the road. If there is a fallow field and a plowed field, he moves it to the fallow field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict the rule that a מת מצוה is buried where it lies. The answer will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a מת מצוה truly acquires its place, it should be buried right there on the road. But the ברייתא says to move it to the side and even choose the less damaging field. So which is it?
steps.confusionAlert: Don't conclude that a מת מצוה doesn't acquire its place. The ברייתא continues in step 30, and רב ביבי resolves the contradiction in step 31.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
One who finds a body lying on a main road

phrases.aramaic: מְפַנֵּהוּ לִימִין אִיסְרַטְיָא אוֹ לִשְׂמֹאל אִיסְרַטְיָא.
phrases.english: moves it to the right of the road or to the left of the road.
If there is a fallow field and a plowed field,
he moves it to the fallow field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule just quoted in step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a מת מצוה acquires its place.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires moving the body off the road and choosing a field, so the body does not stay where it was found.

steps.title: The ברייתא lets you move the body wherever you want
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא from step 29 continues. If you must choose between a plowed field and a sown field, move the body to the plowed one. If both fields are the same kind, move it wherever you wish. This sharpens the contradiction with 'a מת מצוה acquires its place.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If one field is plowed and one is sown, he moves the body to the plowed field. If both are fallow, both plowed, or both sown, he moves it wherever he wants!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא it started in step 29. This completes the challenge against יהושע's rule that a מת מצוה is buried where it is found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא keeps ranking fields by how much damage a grave would cause there. When both fields are the same, it gives full freedom to move the body. That openly contradicts the idea that the body 'acquires its place' and may not be moved.

keyTerms.meaning: A plowed field that has not been planted yet
A sown field with seeds already planted
Fallow fields that are not being worked

phrases.english: A plowed field and a sown field:
phrases.notes: The ברייתא is still listing choices for where to move the body found on the road.

phrases.english: he moves it to the plowed field.
If both of them were fallow;
both plowed; both sown:
he moves it to any place he wants!
phrases.notes: The exclamation mark is the challenge: the body clearly does not 'acquire its place' here.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׂדֵה נִיר וּשְׂדֵה זֶרַע – מְפַנֵּהוּ לִשְׂדֵה נִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted in step 29 and completes its challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: יהושע's condition that a מת מצוה acquires its place (step 28).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lets the body be moved to another field, and even to any place one wishes, so the body does not seem to acquire its place.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about a body lying on the boundary path
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי explains that the ברייתא is talking about a body lying on the boundary path between fields. Since we are already allowed to move it from there, we may move it anywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי said: The ברייתא is about a body lying on the boundary path. Since we are allowed to move it, we may move it to any place we want.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי answers the challenge by limiting the ברייתא to one special case: a body lying on a path.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהושע's rule covers a body found in a field, which stays there. A body lying on a path may be moved, because a grave there would make the path impassable for כהנים. Once moving it is allowed, it may go anywhere, so the ברייתא does not contradict יהושע.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who answers the challenge
The boundary strip or path between fields

phrases.english: Rav Beivai said:
It is about one lying on the boundary path;
since permission was given to move it,
he may move it to any place he wants.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב בִּיבִי: בְּמוּטָּל עַל הַמֵּיצַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from steps 29-30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא is about a body on the path, not in a field.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to allow moving any מת מצוה, which would cancel יהושע's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: A body in a field stays where it is. A body on a path may be moved, and then it may go anywhere.
steps.whatToRemember: A מת מצוה is buried where it is found. The exception is a body lying on a path, which may be moved to any place.

steps.title: The list has eleven conditions, not ten
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא counts יהושע's conditions in the ברייתא and finds eleven, even though the ברייתא said there were ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Ten?! These are eleven!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the opening of the ברייתא, which said יהושע made ten conditions, and challenges the count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list the ברייתא gave actually adds up to eleven items. So either the number ten is wrong, or one item does not belong to יהושע. The next step will explain which.

keyTerms.meaning: They are; they add up to

phrases.english: They said: Ten?!
phrases.notes: This goes back to the opening of the ברייתא, which said יהושע made ten conditions.

phrases.english: These come to eleven!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: עֲשָׂרָה?! הָנֵי חַד סְרֵי הָוְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the discussion of individual conditions and returns to the total count in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that יהושע made ten conditions.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counting the items listed gives eleven, which does not match the number ten.

steps.title: Walking on private paths came from שלמה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the rule letting people walk on private paths was not one of יהושע's conditions. It was said by שלמה, so יהושע's conditions really are ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Walking on private paths: שלמה said it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the counting problem by taking one item off יהושע's list and crediting it to שלמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission to walk through someone's private field on its paths came from שלמה המלך. Once it is removed from יהושע's list, the ten conditions fit the ברייתא's number.

phrases.english: Walking on private paths:
Solomon said it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the counting challenge of step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different source: one item on the list belongs to שלמה, not יהושע.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All eleven items were יהושע's conditions, which contradicts the number ten.
steps.terutzMaskana: Walking on private paths is שלמה's rule, so יהושע made exactly ten conditions.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows שלמה's teaching about letting people cross your field
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports the claim: someone who stops people from crossing his field after his crops are harvested is criticized. The ברייתא applies the verse 'Do not be called bad for failing to be good' to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: If his produce is all harvested from the field and he still does not let people walk through, what do people say about him? 'What does he gain, and what harm are people doing him?' About him the verse says: 'From being good, do not be called bad.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show where שלמה's teaching about walking through fields comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the crops are gone, people crossing the field cause no damage. Blocking them anyway gives the owner nothing and earns him a bad name. The ברייתא connects this to a verse, which is meant to come from שלמה's writings.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
Do not be called bad because you held back from being good

phrases.english: As it is taught:
If his produce was finished from the field,
and he does not let people
enter into his field:
what do people say about him?
"What benefit does so-and-so have,
and what harm are people doing to him?"
About him the verse says:
"From being good, do not be called bad."

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא: הֲרֵי שֶׁכָּלוּ פֵּירוֹתָיו מִן הַשָּׂדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 33's claim that walking on private paths is a teaching of שלמה.
steps.raayaObject: That letting people walk through private fields comes from שלמה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that quotes a verse criticizing someone who blocks people from his harvested field.

steps.title: Is that verse really written anywhere?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the verse 'From being good, do not be called bad' actually appears in תנ"ך, since no such verse exists.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really written: 'From being good, do not be called bad'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's quote, because there is no verse with these exact words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said 'the verse says,' but these words are not found in תנ"ך. So the גמרא wants to know what source the ברייתא really means.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it really written? (a challenge to a quote)

phrases.english: And is it written:
"From being good, do not be called bad"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי כְּתִיב: ״מִהְיוֹת טוֹב אַל תִּקָּרֵי רָע״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the verse quoted in the ברייתא of step 34.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that 'the verse says' these words.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No verse in תנ"ך has these words, so the quote seems to have no source.

steps.title: A verse in משלי says the same idea
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: yes, a verse with the same idea exists in משלי: 'Do not withhold good from those it belongs to, when you are able to do it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, something like it is written: 'Do not withhold good from its owners, when it is in your power to do it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא was quoting the idea of a real verse, not its exact words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in משלי, which שלמה wrote, tells us not to hold back a kindness we are able to give. Letting people walk through a harvested field costs nothing, so refusing goes against this verse. This also supports crediting the rule to שלמה.

keyTerms.meaning: Something like this; along these lines
Do not withhold good from those it belongs to

steps.whatToRemember: Walking on private paths after the harvest is שלמה's teaching, based on 'Do not withhold good' in משלי. That is why יהושע's conditions stay at ten.

phrases.english: Yes, it is written along these lines:
"Do not withhold good from its owners,
phrases.notes: משלי 3:27

phrases.english: when it is in the power of your hand to do it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 35 by pointing to a real verse with the same meaning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Same idea in different words: the ברייתא gave the meaning of a verse in משלי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's quote seemed to have no source in תנ"ך.
steps.terutzMaskana: The source is משלי 3:27, a verse by שלמה, which carries the same message.

steps.title: Isn't רבי יהודה's manure rule another condition?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the number ten by bringing a ברייתא where רבי יהודה says יהושע allowed people to pile manure in the public street for thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are there really no more? But there is רבי יהודה's rule! A ברייתא teaches that רבי יהודה says: during the season for taking out manure, a person may take his manure out to the public street and pile it there for a full thirty days, so that people and animals walk on it. יהושע gave the land to the Jewish people on this condition!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks if the list of ten is too short. It brings a ruling of רבי יהודה that is also described as one of יהושע's conditions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 32 asked whether there were too many conditions. Now the challenge goes the other way: רבי יהודה's ברייתא uses the same phrase, 'on this condition יהושע gave out the land.' So it looks like an eleventh condition that the ten-condition ברייתא left out.

keyTerms.meaning: And is there nothing more? Asks if a list is missing something
But there is! Points to an item that was left out
The season for taking manure out to the fields
Public domain, such as the street
Gave out as an inheritance, here the dividing of ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: And is there nothing more?
But there is the one of Rabbi Yehuda!
As it is taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
At the time of taking out manure,
a person may take his manure out to the public domain
and pile it up for all thirty days,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא נִישּׁוֹף בְּרַגְלֵי אָדָם וּבְרַגְלֵי בְהֵמָה.
phrases.english: so that it gets trampled by the feet of people and the feet of animals.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁעַל מְנָת כֵּן הִנְחִיל יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הָאָרֶץ!
phrases.english: For on this condition Joshua gave the land to Israel!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ לֵיכָּא? וְהָא אִיכָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 32 asked if there were too many conditions. This step asks if there are too few.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that יהושע made exactly ten conditions.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא calls רבי יהודה's manure rule one of יהושע's conditions, so the list should have more than ten.

steps.title: Aren't רבי ישמעאל's three court conditions also missing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a second challenge: רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה lists three 'conditions of the court' about saving another person's property, and he also says יהושע gave out the land on these conditions.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there are also the rules of רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. A ברייתא teaches that he says: It is a condition of the court that a person may go into his friend's field and cut his friend's branch to save his own swarm of bees, and then pay his friend for the branch. It is a condition of the court that a person may pour out his own wine to save his friend's honey, and take the value of his wine out of the honey. It is a condition of the court that a person may unload his own wood and load his friend's flax, and take the value of his wood out of the flax. יהושע gave the land to the Jewish people on these conditions!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings more rules that are also called יהושע's conditions. They come from רבי ישמעאל and are about saving someone else's property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the three cases follows the same pattern: you may harm something of lower value (a branch, your wine, your wood) to save something of higher value (your bees, his honey, his flax), and you get paid back. Since this ברייתא also ends 'on this condition יהושע gave out the land,' the list of ten looks even more incomplete.

keyTerms.meaning: A condition of the court: a rule that applies automatically, even if no one agreed to it

steps.confusionAlert: In the wine and wood cases, the person saving gives up his OWN property to save his friend's more valuable property. He does not lose out, because he is paid back from the property he saved.

phrases.english: And there is the one of Rabbi Yishmael

phrases.aramaic: בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה –
phrases.english: son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka!
As it is taught: Rabbi Yishmael,

phrases.aramaic: בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka, says:
It is a condition of the court

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיְּהֵא זֶה יוֹרֵד לְתוֹךְ שְׂדֵה חֲבֵירוֹ
phrases.english: that this one may go down into his friend's field
and cut off his friend's branch
to save his own swarm of bees,

phrases.aramaic: וְנוֹתֵן לוֹ דְּמֵי שׂוֹכוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ;
phrases.english: and he pays him the value of his friend's branch.
And it is a condition of the court
that this one may pour out his wine
and save his friend's honey,

phrases.aramaic: וְנוֹטֵל דְּמֵי יֵינוֹ מִתּוֹךְ דּוּבְשָׁנוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ;
phrases.english: and he takes the value of his wine from his friend's honey.
And it is a condition of the court
that this one may unload his wood
and load his friend's flax,

phrases.aramaic: וְנוֹטֵל דְּמֵי עֵצָיו מִתּוֹךְ פִּשְׁתָּנוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ;
phrases.english: and he takes the value of his wood from his friend's flax.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁעַל מְנָת כֵּן הִנְחִיל יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הָאָרֶץ!
phrases.english: For on this condition Joshua gave the land to Israel!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אִיכָּא דְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source to the same challenge from step 37.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that יהושע made exactly ten conditions.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי ישמעאל's three court conditions are also linked to יהושע, so they seem to be missing from the list too.

steps.title: The list of ten counts only rules everyone agrees on
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ten-condition ברייתא does not count opinions of single חכמים, like רבי יהודה and רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are not talking about the opinions of individual חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers both challenges at once. The list of ten only includes conditions that all the חכמים accept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules of רבי יהודה and רבי ישמעאל are their own personal opinions, and the other חכמים may not agree. The ברייתא of ten counts only the agreed conditions, so it really does have exactly ten.

keyTerms.meaning: Individuals: opinions of a single חכם that the others don't necessarily share

steps.whatToRemember: יהושע's ten conditions are the ones all the חכמים agree on. Other rules said in his name by single חכמים, like רבי יהודה's manure rule and רבי ישמעאל's rescue rules, are not counted in the ten.

phrases.english: We are not speaking of individual opinions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenges of steps 37 and 38 together.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the list: it counts only rulings everyone agrees on.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any rule that a ברייתא links to יהושע's division of the land should be counted among the ten.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only conditions accepted by all the חכמים are counted. The opinions of single חכמים are left out, so the count of ten stands.
